speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to my office. I understand you are experiencing neck pain, arm pain, paresthesias, and muscle weakness. To help me diagnose the cause of these symptoms, can you tell me how long you have been experiencing them and if the pain radiates in a specific pattern down your arm?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of burning pain in his neck and arms, accompanying paresthesias in his hands. Over the past 3 months, he has experienced increasing weakness in both hands. He has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and hypertension. He was involved in a motor vehicle accident 3 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detailed history; the combination of a one-year history of burning pain, paresthesias, and progressive bilateral hand weakness is concerning for a compressive myelopathy, possibly related to your cervical spine or a systemic issue given your diabetes and hypertension. Have you noticed any difficulty with balance, coordination, or walking? REQUEST IMAGES: Cervical_Spine_MRI

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Burning pain in neck and arms, and weakness in both hands. I also have Paresthesias in hands, Absent reflexes, Decreased hand grip with fasciculations.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS) with superimposed Cervical Spondylotic Myelopathy.

The presence of fasciculations, absent reflexes (lower motor neuron signs) combined with progressive weakness and sensory symptoms (upper motor neuron/pain features) is highly characteristic of ALS. Given your history of trauma and diabetes, please confirm if the weakness has spread to your legs or if you experience difficulty swallowing or speaking.
